mainEntity.name: How do I know if my Los Angeles property is even eligible for an ADU before I spend money on plans?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Most single-family and many multifamily lots in Los Angeles are eligible for at least one ADU, but you need to confirm zoning, setbacks, and access before investing in design. The quickest way is to check your parcel’s zoning and then compare it to your city’s ADU standards. 

ADUs are generally allowed on residentially zoned lots with an existing or proposed main home, but hillside, historic, or small lots can have extra limits. Local rules cover maximum size, height, parking, and where the ADU can sit on the lot.

Key factors:
- Zoning designation and whether ADUs are permitted by-right
- Existing structures (garage, detached buildings, multifamily)
- Lot size, shape, and access for fire and utilities
- Special overlays (hillside, coastal, historic, HOA rules)

Start by pulling your zoning info (often online), then do a quick feasibility review with a designer or ADU contractor before ordering full plans. A reputable builder can usually flag red flags in a short site visit so you don’t waste money on an impossible design.
